text:
sophie: customer on enterprise plan sees intermittent 403s when calling /v1/generate, no obvious request id in their client logs. non-technical helpdesk rep with the customer — can we give them a super minimal set of steps to extract a session identifier from our console or SDK and a curl they can run?

sam: yep. two quick options depending on whether they're using our web console, the embedded SDK, or a mobile/webview. which one is the customer on?

sophie: they say "we use the dashboard to trigger jobs" and occasionally a desktop app that wraps a webview. so start with console + webview. non-dev user, so need super click-for-click.

devin: for console users (non-dev): 1) open app.redwood.com -> top-right avatar -> "Sessions". 2) find the session row nearest to the failing time (there's a "last activity" column). 3) click the row -> Details panel -> Copy "Session hash" (labelled "session_id" in the UI). 4) paste that into a reply to us.

maria: for embedded webview / desktop wrapper: ask them to open the app, then: 1) press Ctrl+Shift+I (or Cmd+Opt+I) to open devtools, 2) go to Network tab, filter by "/v1/generate" (or type "generate"), 3) click the failing request and look in the Headers tab for the header named "x-redwood-session" or a query param "session_id". copy that value.

sam: if they can't open devtools, have them take a screenshot of the network request headers (mask auth tokens) or export a HAR (File -> Save as HAR) and attach it to the ticket. HARs are preferred if they can share.

sophie: once they give the session hash what next?

devin: ask them to run a minimal curl that reproduces the call but with the session header (this doesn't require sharing their auth token with us if they replace it with "REDACTED"). example to give the customer (replace placeholders):

```
curl -v "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Redwood-Session: REPLACE_WITH_SESSION_HASH" -d '{"model":"rw-medium-1","input":"hello"}'
```

devin: If the curl returns a 403 with no body or different error, tell them to add -i to include headers and paste the full response headers. That often shows an internal request id in the response like: `x-redwood-request-id: abc123` we can use.

maria: if they can't run curl, give them a pre-populated snippet they can paste into the browser console to fetch the same endpoint (uses fetch, again replace the token):

```
fetch('https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': 'Bearer REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_TOKEN',
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'X-Redwood-Session': 'REPLACE_WITH_SESSION_HASH'
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({model:'rw-medium-1', input:'hi'})
}).then(r=>r.text()).then(t=>console.log(t)).catch(e=>console.error(e))
```

sophie: good. anything to ask them to include with that session hash to help us correlate quickly?

sam: yes — include: 1) exact local timestamp (with timezone) when the failure happened, 2) the user email (or customer org id), 3) the session hash, 4) a screenshot of the error from their app, 5) the minimal curl output (headers + body), or HAR. Those five items let us find the ingress logs and trace quickly.

devin: also ask them to note whether the failing request used a different region (EU vs US). If they used a private deployment, ask for the deployment name.

maria: internal tip: when they supply the session hash, run our internal correlate CLI: `ri correlate --session SESSION_HASH --since "2026-03-15T00:00:00Z" --until "2026-03-15T01:00:00Z"` — that often surfaces matched request IDs and the backend trace id. (share only with eng on escalation).

sophie: ok i'll send a single compact message to the customer with the click-by-click and the curl.
sam: one more thing — if they can't find a session hash but can provide a screenshot of SDK logs, ask them to search for lines that include `sessionId=`, `req_id=`, or `x-redwood-*`. those substrings are our fastest win.
maria: and remind them to redact tokens when pasting. if they want to share a debug bundle, they can generate it from the console: Settings -> Support -> Export Debug Bundle (includes session metadata, logs, and optional HAR). ask them to attach the bundle to the ticket and confirm they consent to sharing logs.
sophie: perfect, thanks. i'll send now. :thumbsup:
